A fee of two percent of the selling price applies only to kept orders and is fully reversed on returns. Each return costs another twenty dollars to handle, and returned stock has no resale or recovery value. There are no other variable costs; exclude fixed overhead and tax. What is signed expected contribution per original order, in dollars?

follow_up.question: What changes if a returned item has resale value?
follow_up.reference: The returned-order outcome would include the recoverable value, net of any extra recovery costs. That would increase expected contribution relative to the stated assumption that the returned item has no recoverable value.

Each order is sold for 90 dollars and incurs 40 dollars of product and outbound fulfilment cost whether kept or returned. Exactly 20 percent of orders are returned for a full refund. A fee of 10 percent of the selling price applies only to kept orders and is fully reversed on returns. Each return costs another 25 dollars to handle, and returned stock has no resale or recovery value. There are no other variable costs; exclude fixed overhead and tax. What is signed expected contribution per original order, in dollars?
